title: Ensure password history remember is configured
objective: Remediate CIS checkpoint 5.3.3.3.1: Ensure password history remember is configured

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

parameters.name: password_history_remember
parameters.description: Number of previous passwords to remember (pwhistory remember value)

steps.name: Check if pwhistory remember is already configured
steps.function: 1. Verify if the password history remember configuration is already present. Check /etc/security/pwhistory.conf for 'remember = {{ password_history_remember }}' and ensure no 'remember' argument exists in pam_pwhistory.so lines in /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth. If the configuration is already correct, skip remediation and go to step-04 (transform). Otherwise, proceed to step-02 (remediation).

parameters.cmd:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
{
  l_remember="{{ password_history_remember }}"
  l_pwhistory_conf_ok=0
  l_pam_ok=0

  # Check /etc/security/pwhistory.conf
  if grep -Eqs "^\s*remember\s*=\s*${l_remember}\s*$" /etc/security/pwhistory.conf; then
    l_pwhistory_conf_ok=1
  fi

  # Check pam_pwhistory.so lines in system-auth and password-auth
  l_pam_ok=1
  for l_pam_file in system-auth password-auth; do
    l_authselect_file="/etc/authselect/$(head -1 /etc/authselect/authselect.conf | grep 'custom/')/$l_pam_file"
    if grep -Eqs "^\s*password\s+(requisite|required|sufficient)\s+pam_pwhistory\.so.*\s+remember\s*=\s*\S+" "$l_authselect_file"; then
      l_pam_ok=0
    fi
  done

  if [ "$l_pwhistory_conf_ok" -eq 1 ] && [ "$l_pam_ok" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "COMPLIANT"
  else
    echo "NOT_COMPLIANT"
  fi
}

steps.name: Run the provided remediation script to fix Ensure password history remember is configured

parameters.cmd:
#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   l_remember="{{ password_history_remember }}"
   # Set remember in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf
   if grep -Eqs "^\s*remember\s*=" /etc/security/pwhistory.conf; then
     sed -ri "s/^\s*remember\s*=.*/remember = ${l_remember}/" /etc/security/pwhistory.conf
   else
     echo "remember = ${l_remember}" >> /etc/security/pwhistory.conf
   fi

   for l_pam_file in system-auth password-auth; do
     l_authselect_file="/etc/authselect/$(head -1 /etc/authselect/authselect.conf | grep 'custom/')/$l_pam_file"
     sed -ri 's/(^\s*password\s+(requisite|required|sufficient)\s+pam_pwhistory\.so.*)(\s+ remember\s*=\s*\S+)(.*$)/\1\4/' "$l_authselect_file"
   done
   authselect apply-changes
}

reference_procedure:
Edit or add the following line in /etc/security/pwhistory.conf:
remember = 24
Run the following script to remove the remember argument from the pam_pwhistory.so module in /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth:
#!/usr/bin/env bash

{
   for l_pam_file in system-auth password-auth; do
     l_authselect_file="/etc/authselect/$(head -1 /etc/authselect/authselect.conf | grep 'custom/')/$l_pam_file"
     sed -ri 's/(^\s*password\s+(requisite|required|sufficient)\s+pam_pwhistory\.so.*)(\s+ remember\s*=\s*\S+)(.*$)/\1\4/' "$l_authselect_file"
   done
   authselect apply-changes
}
